title: Cross-region affinity, controlled spillover, and sovereign routing for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated capacity across regions and multiple zones need deterministic throughput guarantees and clear data residency controls while preserving availability. Current behavior can cause uncontrolled spillover: when a regional pool is saturated, traffic may be routed to a neighboring region without explicit residency checks or soft-affinity policies, causing compliance and billing surprises.

Goal: Define and implement a placement and failover model that enforces residency constraints, enables soft-affinity (preferred-zone routing with bounded spillover), and integrates with autoscaling to preserve throughput SLOs without violating data-sovereignty policies. Provide operational tooling and telemetry to make decisions auditable and debuggable.

Scope: This ticket focuses on the control-plane placement policy and routing decisions for dedicated fleets (regional and multi-zone). Runtime execution changes (kernel-level optimizations) are out of scope and will be tracked separately.

Design summary: The policy has three orthogonal controls:
1) Residency Lock: an explicit boolean per-customer pool that prevents cross-region routing for requests with residency=locked; requests failing residency checks return 409 with a structured retry hint.
2) Soft Affinity + Spillover Budget: each pool has an affinity weight per zone/region and a spillover budget (percentage of traffic allowed to leave the preferred region when capacity pressure is detected). Spillover is bounded by both budget and remaining SLA headroom.
3) Controlled Failover Strategy: ordered failover groups (primary region -> fallback region A -> fallback region B). Failover occurs only when capacity underprovisioning exceeds a configured threshold and after autoscaling tries fast-shrink/fast-grow windows.

Routing & autoscaling interactions: Routing evaluates (in order): residency lock -> affinity weight -> capacity headroom -> spillover budget -> ordered failover. Autoscaler exposes projected fill rate and a "drain-safe" flag to routing to avoid moving traffic during active drains. When a spillover decision is made, requests include an opaque header so downstream billing and auditing can attribute non-resident execution.

Operational controls: Admin UI controls for pool owners to set residency, affinity weights, spillover %, ordered failover list, and emergency override. Console will surface per-pool spillover events, SLA impact, and cost delta for cross-region execution.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Residency-locked pools never route to regions outside the approved list (e2e test). 2) Soft-affinity honors zone weights and does not exceed configured spillover budget under synthetic load. 3) Failover ordering respected and documented in logs and console. 4) Autoscaler signals are consumed to avoid routing oscillation: at least one e2e test covering a simulated drain + autoscale response. 5) Billing attribution header present on spillover requests and visible in tracing. 6) Dashboard surfaces spillover volume and SLA impact with <5s query latency.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged control-plane rollout to canary cluster (10% of control-plane nodes) with no default spillover (spillover=0). 2) Run canary for 3 days with traffic mirroring and synthetic load tests. 3) Enable spillover with conservative defaults (spillover=5%) for internal customers and monitor. 4) Gradual ramp to customers on request and per-tenant opt-in for residency looser policies. 5) Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics and sign-off from Security and SRE.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation logic; integration tests between routing, autoscaler, and billing attribution header; chaos test that simulates zone outage and validates ordered failover; compliance test that asserts residency-locked behavior returns 409 and does not leak telemetry to other regions. Include load tests measuring throughput and p99 latency under spillover enabled/disabled scenarios.
monitoring_and_metrics: New metrics: dedicated.pool.spillover.count, dedicated.pool.spillover.bytes, dedicated.pool.spillover_cost_delta_usd, dedicated.pool.residency_violations, dedicated.pool.failover_events, dedicated.routing.decision_latency_ms. Dashboards: per-pool time-series for spillover %, capacity headroom, autoscaler projected_fill, and SLA breach rate. Alerts: >=5% of requests for a residency-locked pool routed off-region in 5m window -> P0 alert; sustained p99 latency degradation >20% post-spillover -> P1.
